A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same work. Shared methods, theorems, and figures can be matched across reflow, and the complete appendices are available: A–G in v1 and A–H in v2.

before.justification: Sections 3.2 and 4.2 report original centroid-recovery simulations. Appendices F–G include dimensionality studies and softmax-attention experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulations in Figures 1–9, including the higher-dimensional and softmax experiments in Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: Section 6 introduces Tctx, a linear attention encoder using identity query/key/value matrices, equivalently d orthogonal heads, without learned attention parameters. This substantially extends v1's proposed methods beyond the retained trained two-head encoders.

E1.justification: Empirical coverage remains the same synthetic Dirac and Gaussian mixtures, noise regimes, and dimensionality studies. The new setting with sequence-specific random centroids is analyzed mathematically without new training or evaluation experiments.

E2.justification: The empirical studies retain the same linear and softmax attention variants, with no added or removed experimental baseline. The oracle quantizer was already a theoretical reference in v1.

E3.justification: Appendices E–G retain the experimental settings, including sequence length 30, batch size 256, learning rate 0.01, initialization procedures, iteration budgets, regularization grids, and distance/RMSE metrics.

E4.justification: The same initialization comparisons, regularization sweeps, noise sensitivity, and dimensionality analyses remain in Figures 1–9. No new empirical ablation, robustness test, or case study is added.

E5.justification: The reported independent-run counts and 95% percentile-interval practice are unchanged. The newly derived conditional variances describe theoretical properties of the encodings, rather than changes to experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical plots in Figures 1–9 are unchanged. Appendix G.2 nevertheless removes the qualitative finding that softmax is less robust than its linear counterpart, retaining only the finding that alignment worsens as noise and dimensionality increase.

T1.justification: Proposition 5.1 gains conditional-variance results supported by new Proposition C.2. Section 6 and Appendix H introduce random-centroid assumptions and derive the new encoder's risk, expectation, and variance. Section 5 also corrects the oracle-risk ratio from 1 − 2/σ² to 1 − 2/d.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion now claim that attention with no learned parameters performs approximate in-context quantization for sequence-specific mixture centroids. In-context clustering appeared only as future work in v1.

C2.justification: Section 5 expands the quantization interpretation through conditional variance, unequal admissible output classes, and a risk advantage that shrinks with dimension. Section 6 adds substantial discussion of rank limitations for varying centroids and the applicability of the new encoder.

D1.justification: The PSGD update descriptions, JAX disclosure, hyperparameters, centroid definitions, and runtime estimates in Appendices E–G are retained. No new implementation instructions or code/data access information are supplied.

R1.justification: The cited works and the positioning against prior supervised Transformer clustering work, particularly He et al. (2025), remain unchanged. Citation punctuation changes are editorial.

P1.justification: Existing text is largely retained. Local changes include expanded quantization explanations, rewritten Appendix D statements, relocation of v1's Appendix C.3 to B.3, and insertion of Section 6 before the conclusion. Affiliation, acknowledgments, and citation style are also updated.

P2.justification: All nine figures retain their graphical content. Figure 3 now sits beside wrapped prose, other figures move during reflow, and some revised Section 5 prose appears in blue. No figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the quantization argument by correcting the inconsistent risk ratio and supplementing mean alignment with explicit variance guarantees and supporting derivations. Section 6 and Appendix H also establish a varying-centroid capability that v1 left as future work. These gains improve mathematical precision and explanatory support; evidence for the new setting remains theoretical.
